sections.h2: Where do you pay and question property tax in Lowndes County?
sections.html:
Lowndes County runs its property tax out of Valdosta, with the commissioner and the assessors answering different questions. Bills, payments and liens go through the commissioner. Values and special assessment programs go through the assessors.

  • Lowndes County Tax Commissioner: 300 N. Patterson Street, P.O. Box 1409, Valdosta, GA 31601. Phone 229-671-2579, fax 229-671-2599. The lobby keeps weekday hours of 8:00 AM until 4:45 PM, and the drive-thru lane runs from 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM.
  • Lowndes County Board of Tax Assessors: phone (229) 671-2540.
  • Clerk of Superior Court deed room, Lowndes County Judicial Complex, 327 N. Ashley Street, first floor: copies of your warranty deed.

A drive-up drop box sits in the front parking lot of the Government Building, on the right-hand side. If you mail a check, write the bill number on it. Add a stamped return envelope if you want a receipt back.

sections.h2: What is Lowndes County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Lowndes sits in south Georgia and covers about 497 square miles of land. The Census Bureau estimates 122,867 residents for July 1, 2025, a gain of 3.9% over the 2020 base of 118,259. That pace is slower than Lumpkin County's 8.0% and far slower than Long County's 33.5%.

QuickFacts counts 54,425 housing units and reports 237.8 residents for each square mile in 2020. About 57 of every 100 occupied homes (56.9%) are owner-occupied, and a typical owner-occupied house is worth $215,600 in the 2020 to 2024 survey. Household income runs $58,541 at the midpoint, and 18.1% of residents live in poverty. Valdosta-area commutes are short at 19.5 minutes, the briefest among the four Georgia places in this set.

The county issued 804 building permits in 2025. Retail sales reached about $2.64 billion in 2022, and medical and social service receipts were near $1.07 billion that year, which points to a regional hub economy instead of a bedroom county.

sections.h2: When are Lowndes County property taxes due, and what do late payments cost?
sections.html:
Real estate and business personal property tax is generally due by November 15 each year. The commissioner mails bills at least 60 days ahead of that date, and the county's tax information page says the mailing happens in the first week of October.

Lowndes County property tax calendar and late charges, as the tax commissioner publishes them
ItemWhat the commissioner's site says
Property returnsFiled January 1 through April 1
Homestead applicationMust arrive by April 1 to count that year
Appeal of assessment45 days from the date of the assessment notice
Due date, real estateGenerally November 15; a weekend or holiday moves to the next business day
Interest after due dateBank prime rate plus 3%, added monthly
Penalty5% of tax due once 120 days pass, repeated every 120 days, capped at 20%
Penalty exceptionHomesteaded property with a bill under $500.00
Lien (FiFa)Recorded on the General Execution Docket if the bill stays unpaid

Source: Lowndes County Tax Commissioner FAQ and tax bill information pages.

A mailed payment needs a postmark dated no later than the due date. The commissioner also lets owners pay in two installments, though interest and penalty attach to whatever remains open after the due date. Since the date can shift, the office tells owners to trust the date printed on the bill itself.

sections.h2: How do assessments and appeals work in Lowndes County?
sections.html:
Georgia taxes 40% of fair market value, and the Lowndes assessors set that value every year. An owner may file a return between January 1 and April 1 declaring a proposed value. If the Board of Assessors disagrees, it mails a notice with its own number, and the county's tax information page puts those notices in May.

To contest the number, count 45 days from the date printed on the notice. The appeal goes to the Lowndes County Board of Equalization or to an arbitrator. After a ruling, you can continue to Superior Court by mailing or filing a written notice with the assessors.

  • Value disputes start with the assessors at (229) 671-2540.
  • Billing disputes start with the commissioner at 229-671-2579.
  • A mill equals one dollar of tax for each $1,000 of assessed value. The county commissioners and the Board of Education each vote a rate yearly.

Once value is settled, exemptions come off the assessed figure and the millage rate multiplies what is left. For the actual Lowndes rate, read your current bill, because it changes from year to year.

sections.h2: What payment options does the Lowndes County commissioner list?
sections.html:
Owners can pay at the counter, by mail, in the drive-up box, or by credit card. The office states that the card company charges a convenience fee: 2.57% on Discover, Mastercard and Visa, and 3% on American Express, with a $1.50 minimum on each.

The office does not mail past-due bills every month, only at certain intervals, so confirm the amount due before you send money. Interest keeps adding each month until the balance clears, and the commissioner's page says a lien stays on a credit record for at least seven years.

If taxes stay unpaid beyond 90 days after the due date, the county's tax information page says the Delinquent Tax Office may begin tax sale proceedings. Ask the commissioner before that point about the exact balance and your options.

sections.h2: What happens if you sell a Lowndes County house with tax still unpaid?
sections.html:
The bill is built around whoever held title on January 1. A lien gets recorded in that person's name unless the commissioner receives a contract or closing statement, within 90 days of the due date, showing that the new owner took on the tax. Sellers who prorated the tax at closing should bring a copy of that statement to the Patterson Street office.

State guidance is plain: the person who owned the property on January 1 owes that year's ad valorem tax in full, with no refund for a January 2 sale. A buyer can still be billed too, since the commissioner mails a bill to the new owner once the deed transfer reaches the office.

If a bill arrives for a house you already sold, forward it to the new owner. An inherited or tenant-occupied house follows the same path: request a payoff from the commissioner, then let the closing attorney settle it at the table.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and special programs reduce Lowndes County tax?
sections.html:
The homestead exemption is the usual one for a residence, and the freeport exemption is the usual one for business personal property. You must own and live in the home as of January 1, and you apply at the Tax Assessor's Office.

  • Applications are accepted all year, but the office must have yours by April 1 for it to count that year. Later ones roll to the next year.
  • Once granted, the exemption continues in the same house. A move means a new application for the new address.
  • At age 65, an owner can apply for an additional homestead exemption, according to the commissioner's FAQ.
  • Special assessment programs, such as farm and conservation use, are explained by the assessors.

Mobile and modular homes count as personal property, and the commissioner's FAQ says the owner of any such home located in the county must file a return.

faqs.q: When does Lowndes County property tax come due?
faqs.a: Generally November 15 each year for real estate and business personal property. Read the date on your own bill, because the commissioner says it can change.

faqs.q: What penalty applies to late Lowndes County property tax?
faqs.a: Interest runs at the bank prime rate plus 3% each month, and a 5% penalty lands 120 days after the due date, repeating every 120 days up to 20%. Homesteaded property with a bill under $500.00 escapes the penalty.

faqs.q: Can a Lowndes County owner split the tax bill into two payments?
faqs.a: Yes. The commissioner's office allows two payments, but interest and penalty apply to any balance left after the due date.

faqs.q: Where can I get a copy of my Lowndes County deed?
faqs.a: The Clerk of Superior Court, on the first floor of the Lowndes County Judicial Complex at 327 N. Ashley Street in Valdosta, supplies copies of a warranty deed.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to dispute a Lowndes County assessment?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the date on the assessment notice. Appeal to the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator, and you may continue to Superior Court by written notice to the assessors.
